questions.problem:
If the solid region $R$ is given by 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x-1)^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 1,\,y\ge 0,\,1\le z\le 2\},
$$

then ${∭}_{R}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}V=$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14247307/assets/603dc3142d8329fd9ff9fe8d09b131fe09497405f761918d59261fde314772c6.png)

The region $R$ is one-half of a right vertical cylinder of radius $1$ whose axis passes through the point $(1,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=1,$ and

- bounded above by $z=2.$

With that in mind, let's now write the $(x-1)^{2}+{y}^{2}=1$ in polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2}+{y}^{2} & =1 \\ (r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -1)^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2} & =1 \\ {r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +1+{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )-2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ {r}^{2}-2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ r(r-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $r$ cannot be identical to zero on the entire semicircle, we must have $r=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le 2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,1\le z\le 2\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}((r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2})\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{3}\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}4x\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the cylinder ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4$ for $x\ge 0,$ $y\ge 0$ and between the surfaces $z=0$ and $z=y+3.$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14247307/assets/021047e8d472a91eeeb7b45d239a1577cb7b03c873e0cb7f20ddd5ca0b69b1a3.png)

The region $R$ is a right vertical cylinder of radius $2$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=0,$ and

- bounded above by $z=y+3=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +3.$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le 2,\,0\le \theta <\frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le z\le r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +3\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}4x\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}4r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +3}4{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2}4{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta [z]_{z=0}^{z=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2}4{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta (r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +3)\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2}4{r}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +12{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2}2{r}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta +12{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{[\frac{1}{2}{r}^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta +4{r}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ]}_{r=0}^{r=2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{1}{2}(2)^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta +4(2)^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}8\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta +32\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =[-4\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +32\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]_{\theta =0}^{\theta =\pi /2} \\  & =-4(-1-1)+32(1-0)) \\  & =40.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the cylinder ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4$ for $y\le 0,$ between the surfaces $z=0$ and $z={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+9.$ Express the following triple integral in cylindrical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}}\,\text{d}V
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14247307/assets/350b2dc98a09957c17f1ab629e21021c30fcccd9443068c722fe7565f04dcbfe.png)

The region $R$ is one-half of a right vertical cylinder of radius $2$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=0,$ and

- bounded above by $z={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+9={r}^{2}+9.$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le 2,\,\pi \le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le z\le {r}^{2}+9\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{1}{\sqrt{(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}+1}}\cdot r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{r}{\sqrt{{r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +1}}\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{r}{\sqrt{{r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+1}}\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{r}^{2}+9}\frac{r}{\sqrt{{r}^{2}+1}}\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the cylinder ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1$ and between the surfaces $z=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}$ and $z=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14247307/assets/f4c6f3acefa5d89fd5064de469952da3d68d379559bb4a6a4990a2ea24e4f861.png)

The region $R$ is a right vertical cylinder of radius $1$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by  $z=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}=\sqrt{{r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }=r,$  and

- bounded above by $z=1.$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le 1,\,0\le \theta <2\pi ,\,r\le z\le 1\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}({(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}^{2}+{(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2})\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{r}^{1}{r}^{3}\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}{r}^{3}[z]_{z=r}^{z=1}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}{r}^{3}(1-r)\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}{r}^{3}-{r}^{4}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{[\frac{1}{4}{r}^{4}-\frac{1}{5}{r}^{5}]}_{r=0}^{r=1}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{1}{20}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={[\frac{1}{20}\theta ]}_{\theta =0}^{\theta =2\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{20}(2\pi -0) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14247307/assets/2f36451290eda3db5221e1a5fdbc1647bbedafa97cd47e22d5523d457c4cb83e.png)

The region $R$ is one-half of a right vertical cylinder of radius $2$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,-2)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=0,$ and

- bounded above by $z=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}=r.$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+(y+2)^{2}=4$ in polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+(y+2)^{2} & =4 \\ (r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2)^{2} & =4 \\ {r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +4r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +4 & =4 \\ {r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+4r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ {r}^{2}+4r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ r(r+4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $r$ cannot be identical to zero on the entire semicircle, we must have $r=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le -4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\frac{3\pi }{2}\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le z\le r\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}z({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}z({(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}^{2}-{(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2})\cdot r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}{r}^{3}z({cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{-4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\int }_{0}^{r}{r}^{3}z\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta \,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
